handoff.purpose: Define the task set and helpers for the distillation eval, including the contract that correctness tasks are never graded by slice recall.

symbols.name: AGENT_ENV_ROOT
symbols.note: str; parents[2] of this file; used as repo root for 'agent_env'.

symbols.name: resolve_task_repo
symbols.note: Maps repo label to absolute path; supports 'agent_env', absolute existing paths, and registered project names; raises ValueError otherwise.

symbols.name: CORRECTNESS_KEYS
symbols.note: Tuple ('fail_to_pass', 'pass_to_pass'); presence of either marks a correctness task.

symbols.name: is_correctness_task
symbols.note: Returns True if task is a dict containing any correctness key; presence-based, not truthiness.

symbols.name: task_project_label
symbols.note: Returns project bucket for filtering; '<unknown>' if repo missing; 'agent_env' for agent_env or AGENT_ENV_ROOT; else repo value.

symbols.name: TASKS
symbols.note: list[dict]; slice-recall tasks; first half of list present in this chunk (web_api_file through garden_watering_plan).

claims.text: Each task targets a real symbol/file in a small repo and records the symbols a *sufficient* distilled slice MUST carry to reason about that target.
claims.why: The tasks in this chunk do target files/symbols, but whether the must_include lists are truly 'sufficient' cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: The labels below were picked by reading the code and VERIFIED reachable by running ``semantic_slice`` (see ``daedalus.eval.harness``); a label is only listed if a competent answer about the target genuinely needs it AND it is a real dependency or caller in the neighborhood.
claims.why: Requires running semantic_slice and inspecting the referenced files; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Task shape: { "id": ..., "repo": ..., "target": ..., "must_include": ..., "question": ..., "answer_contains": ..., "label_provenance": ..., "tier": ... }
claims.why: The tasks in this chunk all have these keys (id, repo, target, must_include, question, answer_contains, label_provenance, tier).

claims.text: Honesty note: ``must_include`` items are matched as substrings against the slice text.
claims.why: Scoring behavior is in harness._recall, not in this chunk.

claims.text: For a symbol target the slice is 1-hop (the focus symbol's direct callees/callers), so we only label symbols reachable within that hop -- we do NOT claim transitive callees-of-callees are present when they are not.
claims.why: Depends on semantic_slice behavior, not present here.

claims.text: "hand_reachable"   -- a human picked the label AND verified it reachable by running ``semantic_slice``. This is CIRCULAR: the slicer chose what it is graded on.
claims.why: All tasks in this chunk have label_provenance 'hand_reachable', but verification requires running semantic_slice.

claims.text: Every task below is this provenance today.
claims.why: All tasks in this chunk have label_provenance 'hand_reachable'.

claims.text: Recall computed over ``hand_reachable`` tasks is an upper bound / sanity check, NOT independent proof the slicer works -- ``report.py`` says so on every render, and ``harness.run_tier1`` never blends it with the other provenances into one number.
claims.why: References report.py and harness.run_tier1, which are not in this chunk.

claims.text: "independent_diff" -- labels derived from what an on-disk diff LITERALLY changed, with no graph walk involved. Independent of the slicer.
claims.why: No such tasks in this chunk; mechanism is in mint, not here.

claims.text: "temporal_churn"    -- labels derived from git co-change (files that change together), surfacing edges the static import graph doesn't have. Independent of the slicer.
claims.why: No such tasks in this chunk; mechanism is in mint, not here.

claims.text: ``tier``: "primary" tasks count toward any go/no-go recall number. "quarantine" tasks are minted but not yet confirmed -- ``harness.run_tier1`` excludes them from every headline/aggregate and reports them separately
claims.why: All tasks in this chunk are tier 'primary'; quarantine handling is in harness.run_tier1.

claims.text: Everything above grades the SLICER: ``must_include`` is scored by substring containment in a distilled context slice (``harness._recall``). That measures retrieval, and it is honest about it -- but it never looks at a patch, so no number derived from it can say whether a CHANGE is correct, and an empty ``must_include`` scores 1.0 vacuously.
claims.why: harness._recall is not in this chunk; the scoring behavior cannot be verified here.

claims.text: ``daedalus.eval.correctness`` adds a second, disjoint format that grades the CHANGE, on the SWE-bench pattern, using this repo's own pytest as the oracle
claims.why: correctness.py is not in this chunk.

claims.text: a correctness task carries no ``must_include``
claims.why: The correctness format example in the docstring has no must_include, but the actual task list in this chunk has no correctness tasks to confirm this invariant.

claims.text: scoring one with ``harness._recall`` would return the vacuous 1.0 -- a task that cannot fail, silently inflating the very number the tier machinery exists to keep honest.
claims.why: Depends on harness._recall implementation, not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``is_correctness_task`` below is the single predicate that decides
claims.why: is_correctness_task is defined in this chunk and is the only predicate visible here that identifies correctness tasks.

claims.text: ``harness.eval_task_tier1``/``eval_task_arms`` refuse such a task loudly (an ERRORED row, which ``run_gate`` reports and fails on for a primary tier) instead of grading it.
claims.why: harness and run_gate are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Correctness tasks live in their own store (``correctness.DEFAULT_CORPUS_PATH``) and never enter ``harness.all_tasks()``.
claims.why: correctness.DEFAULT_CORPUS_PATH and harness.all_tasks are not in this chunk.

claims.text: "agent_env" -> this harness repo (dogfood target)
claims.why: resolve_task_repo returns AGENT_ENV_ROOT for 'agent_env', and AGENT_ENV_ROOT is parents[2] of this file, which is the harness repo.

claims.text: a registered name -> daedalus.projects.resolve_repo_root (e.g. sunny_garden)
claims.why: resolve_task_repo calls resolve_repo_root(None, repo) when repo in list_projects().

claims.text: an absolute path -> used as-is (temp fixtures in tests)
claims.why: resolve_task_repo returns repo as-is if os.path.isabs(repo) and Path(repo).exists().

claims.text: Deliberately keyed on the PRESENCE of the field, not on its truthiness: a task with ``"fail_to_pass": []`` is a correctness task with an empty (and therefore invalid, see ``correctness.validate_task``) test list, NOT a slice-recall task -- and it must never be handed to ``_recall``, which would score its absent ``must_include`` as a vacuous 1.0.
claims.why: is_correctness_task uses `any(k in task for k in CORRECTNESS_KEYS)`, which is presence-based, not truthiness.

claims.text: A task with NO ``repo`` key labels as ``"<unknown>"`` rather than raising ``KeyError``.
claims.why: task_project_label uses task.get('repo'), and returns '<unknown>' when repo is None.

claims.text: This function is called from ``harness._task_error_row``, i.e. on the REPORTING path for a task that is already known to be malformed, so a raise here turned "one bad task is reported as a degraded row" into "the whole eval run dies on it" -- the exact failure ``_task_error_row`` exists to prevent. Found by a test, not by reading.
claims.why: harness._task_error_row is not in this chunk; the context of the call cannot be verified here.

claims.text: All Tier-1 labels verified reachable against the current slices -- which is exactly the circularity documented above.
claims.why: Requires running the slicer against the current slices; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Every task is "hand_reachable" / "primary" until an "independent_diff" or "temporal_churn" minter (see daedalus.eval.mint, a separate track) adds tasks with independent labels.
claims.why: All tasks in this chunk have label_provenance 'hand_reachable' and tier 'primary'.

claims.text: Updated when neighborhood expansion moved off the python-only dotted module map onto idx["import_edges"] (S2): ``_py_maps`` no longer exists, and its role -- supplying the lookup semantic_slice expands through -- is now ``_reverse_edges``. Ground truth follows the code; the symbol is still a real callee, verified against the call graph.
claims.why: Requires inspecting slice.py and the call graph; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Updated by the HONEST DENOMINATOR change (slice.py::_whole_repo_tokens): the primary path is now idx["total_tokens"] (tokenizer-measured, carried through by build_index); total_chars // 4 survives only as the fallback for an index dict that predates the field. The label tested total_chars unconditionally and was never updated when the code it grades moved off that formula -- ground truth follows the code (see the comment above this task).
claims.why: Requires inspecting slice.py; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Updated when the per-file pass was extracted into perfile.py and parallelized: build_index no longer calls extract_units/file_metrics/python_imports directly -- they moved behind _per_file_pass. These are its real current dependencies, verified against the call graph. The slicer was NOT the thing that changed; the labels were stale.
claims.why: Requires inspecting index.py and the call graph; not verifiable from this chunk.

observations.what: AGENT_ENV_ROOT is computed as parents[2] of this file; the module docstring explicitly states this. If the file is moved, the constant becomes wrong.
The module docstring makes several claims about harness/correctness/report behavior that are not checkable from this chunk; they should be verified against those modules.
The TASKS list in this chunk contains only slice-recall tasks with label_provenance 'hand_reachable' and tier 'primary', matching the docstring's claim that every task is currently that provenance.
resolve_task_repo returns repo as-is for any existing absolute path, without normalizing; this matches the docstring 'used as-is'.
is_correctness_task is presence-based, not truthiness-based, as documented; this prevents empty fail_to_pass lists from being misclassified.
task_project_label returns '<unknown>' for missing repo and 'agent_env' for both 'agent_env' and AGENT_ENV_ROOT, as documented.
The chunk ends mid-list; the remaining tasks (e.g., garden_watering_plan and beyond) are not fully visible, so any claim about the complete TASKS list is uncheckable.
